arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Arthur Fergenson argued the manufacturer lacked New Jersey contacts.
He stated the company did not direct activity toward New Jersey residents.
He claimed the distributor acted without the manufacturer’s knowledge.

Justice Kagan pressed the advocate on the scope of U. S. targeting. She asked if selling in the U. S. means selling in every state. She noted the United States consists of fifty distinct states. She questioned if the manufacturer wanted to sell in each one. Justice Scalia warned that broad jurisdiction could apply to any American manufacturer.
